```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`tsinferR` infers tree sequences (ancestral recombination graphs) from
genetic variation data. It is a native R implementation of the
[tsinfer](https://tskit.dev/tsinfer) pipeline: the compiled `tsinfer` and
`tskit` C libraries are bundled with the package and no Python installation
is needed.

```{r}
library(tsinferR)
```

## Input data: VCF Zarr

The pipeline reads genotypes from VCF Zarr (VCZ) stores, the format written
by [bio2zarr](https://sgkit-dev.github.io/bio2zarr/). `tsinferR` contains its
own Zarr engine and a VCF converter, so a VCF file can be converted directly:

```{r}
vcf <- system.file("extdata", "example.vcf.gz", package = "tsinferR")
work <- file.path(tempdir(), "tsinferR-vignette")
dir.create(work, showWarnings = FALSE)
samples <- vcf_to_vcz(vcf, file.path(work, "samples.vcz"), overwrite = TRUE)
zarr_list(samples)
dim(zarr_read(samples, "call_genotype"))
```

The example contains 5 diploid individuals. For real data, the
ancestral alleles usually come from an INFO field (use
`vcf_to_vcz(ancestral_info = "AA")`) or a separate store.

## Configuring the pipeline

A configuration describes the input sources, where to find the ancestral
alleles, where to write the ancestors, and how each source is matched:

```{r}
cfg <- tsinfer_config(
  sources = list(tsinfer_source(samples, name = "samples")),
  ancestral_state = ancestral_state(samples, is_reference = TRUE),
  ancestors = list(ancestors_config("ancestors", file.path(work, "ancestors.vcz"), "samples")),
  match = match_config(sources = list(
    ancestors = match_source_config(node_flags = 0, create_individuals = FALSE),
    samples = match_source_config()
  )),
  post_process = post_process_config()
)
```

The same configuration can be written as a TOML file (the format used by the
`tsinfer` command-line tool) and read with `read_config()`.

## Running the inference

`run_tsinfer()` runs all stages:

```{r}
unlink(file.path(work, "ancestors.vcz"), recursive = TRUE)
ts <- run_tsinfer(cfg, num_threads = 2)
ts
```

The stages can also be run one by one:

```{r}
unlink(file.path(work, "ancestors.vcz"), recursive = TRUE)
infer_ancestors(cfg$sources$samples, cfg$ancestors[[1]], cfg$ancestral_state)
raw <- match_haplotypes(cfg)
final <- post_process(raw, cfg)
ts_equals(final, ts)
```

## Inspecting the result

Tables are available as data frames, with JSON metadata decoded:

```{r}
nodes <- ts_nodes(ts)
head(nodes[nodes$flags == 1, c("flags", "time", "individual")])
nodes$metadata[[which(nodes$flags == 1)[1]]]
ts_num_trees(ts)
```

The inferred tree sequence encodes the input genotypes exactly:

```{r}
G <- ts_genotype_matrix(ts)
input <- zarr_read(samples, "call_genotype")
pos <- zarr_read(samples, "variant_position")
input <- matrix(aperm(input, c(1, 3, 2)), nrow = length(pos))
inferred_sites <- match(ts_sites(ts)$position, pos)
all(G == input[inferred_sites, ])
```

## Saving and interoperability

Tree sequences are saved in the standard `.trees` format. The optional
`tskitR` package can read the result directly:

```{r, eval=requireNamespace("tskitR", quietly = TRUE)}
path <- file.path(work, "inferred.trees")
ts_dump(ts, path)
tskit_sequence <- as_tskit(ts)
tskit_sequence$num_trees
ts_equals(ts, as_tsinfer(tskit_sequence))
```

With `tsdateR` installed, the inferred genealogy can also be dated using a
mutation rate. `date_tsinfer()` handles the standard-file bridge and returns
the dated result in tsinferR form:

```{r, eval=requireNamespace("tsdateR", quietly = TRUE)}
dated <- date_tsinfer(ts, mutation_rate = 1e-8)
head(ts_nodes(dated))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
unlink(work, recursive = TRUE)
```
